messages:
elena-support: FYI customer reported a weird reauth loop after they rotated their SSO password. Happening only in iOS app webview (Sentry session: 89f3a). They say MFA keeps prompting even after successful SSO flow. @sam-eng can you triage?

sam-eng: got it. any reproduction steps from the customer? device model / app version?

elena-support: Customer (AcmeCorp) repro steps:
1) Sign in via SSO on desktop (chrome) -> works.
2) Admin rotates password for user.
3) User opens iOS app -> sees SSO sign-in, enters creds, completes MFA, but app immediately prompts for MFA again. Repeat forever.
They tested on iOS 16.5, app v2.4.1. Android unaffected.

maya-sre: quick thought: sounds like session cookie out-of-sync with refresh token rotation, webview not sending cross-site cookie so server thinks device_trust cookie still valid but token mismatch causes forced MFA. Any logs?

elena-support: customer sent two snippets: one from iOS WebView network inspector and one from our auth logs. pasted below.

elena-support: (iOS webview request)
```
POST /oauth/callback HTTP/1.1
Host: auth.redwood.example
Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...; device_trust=dt_v1_abc123; __Host-Refresh=rt_v2_xyz
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
```

elena-support: (server Set-Cookie response observed)
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Set-Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=3600
Set-Cookie: device_trust=dt_v1_abc123; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=1209600
Set-Cookie: __Host-Refresh=rt_v3_new; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=1209600
Location: /app
```

sam-eng: aha — device_trust has SameSite=Lax while refresh token uses None. iOS webviews often treat SameSite=Lax differently for cross-origin POSTs to the auth domain during SSO redirect flow. If device_trust isn't sent back on the POST (or is ambiguous), we might be hitting a server codepath that tries to validate device_trust against the new refresh token and fails, triggering an MFA prompt and a refresh that rotates cookies again. That could loop.

diego-auth: adding server log trace for that session id (redacted):
```
[2026-03-05T14:02:12Z] TRACE trace=89f3a auth.callback start, incoming cookies: session=..., device_trust=dt_v1_abc123
[2026-03-05T14:02:12Z] INFO trace=89f3a refresh.rotate old=rt_v2_xyz new=rt_v3_new
[2026-03-05T14:02:12Z] WARN trace=89f3a device_trust mismatch for user u-123: cookie_version=v1 token_binding=missing
[2026-03-05T14:02:12Z] INFO trace=89f3a issuing mfa_challenge redirect=/mfa?reason=token_mismatch
```

maya-sre: that 'token_binding=missing' smells like webview failing to attach some auth header or attribute we use to bind device_trust to refresh token. We should confirm whether the iOS webview strips cross-site cookies when redirecting from SSO provider -> auth.redwood. Also check cookie attributes across our two domains (auth.redwood.example vs app.redwood.example).

elena-support: customer also noted behaviour: if they fully quit the app and clear app cache then sign in again it's fine. So a cold start works, warm app doesn't.

sam-eng: reproduction plan I can run: emulate iOS webview flow using curl + manually crafted cookies to hit /oauth/callback and see server behaviour. If we can reproduce, fix could be server-side: on password rotation detect refresh-token rotation and proactively clear device_trust cookie / force full reauth (instead of presenting MFA challenge).

sam-eng: repro curl (will run in staging):
```
# simulate SSO callback with stale device_trust + rotated refresh cookie
curl -i -X POST 'https://auth.staging.redwood.example/oauth/callback' -H "Cookie: session=old_session; device_trust=dt_v1_abc123; __Host-Refresh=rt_v2_xyz" -d "code=abc123&state=st-1"
```

sam-eng: expected server response in loop case: 302 -> Set-Cookie rotate refresh + redirect to /mfa, but client then POSTs again with same stale dt cookie which causes rotate -> redirect ...

diego-auth: quick patch idea: on refresh token rotation we mark a short-lived server-side binding key (device_trust_binding_id). If cookie device_trust binding doesn't match, server should clear device_trust cookie and redirect user to interactive reauth page with clear instructions rather than an MFA challenge. That would break loop immediately.

maya-sre: agree. Also we should unify SameSite attributes: set device_trust to SameSite=None (we already do that for refresh in most places). Then test on iOS WebView specifically. But changing SameSite may have security review implications; need product sign-off.

elena-support: customer asked for workaround while we investigate. I suggested they fully quit app and try cold start, which they confirmed works. They asked for a less disruptive step for end users.

sam-eng: interim workaround we can offer: ask users to clear app cookies (settings -> Clear web data) or sign out completely and sign in again. I'll prepare a short KB snippet.

auth-bot: Incident checklist updated: add regression test for iOS webview SSO flow, ensure device_trust SameSite=None is covered, add unit test for refresh rotation -> device_trust mismatch path to clear cookie. (ticket #ENG-2309) :white_check_mark:

diego-auth: I'll draft a safe server-side guard: detect rotation and clear cookie with Set-Cookie device_trust=; Path=/; Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None then redirect to /reauth?reason=rotated_refresh. Want me to put up a PR for canary?

sam-eng: yes please. Run canary behind feature flag and we can enable for a subset of mobile traffic. Also add extra logging to capture user-agent and webview type.

elena-support: ETA for customer update?

sam-eng: I'll have a canary PR today, deploy to staging for validation tomorrow, rollout to canary mobile users in 48h pending tests.

elena-support: great — I'll respond to customer with workaround + note we'll follow up once canary passes.

maya-sre: add to postmortem queue if we see >10 escalations. For now set alert: SSO:auth.callback.mfa_loop_count > 5 in 10m -> notify oncall.

elena-support: thanks team. I'll keep thread updated with customer confirmations.
